paths.description: Homepage: primary headline discovery, global navigation, personalization/ad surface, and site-wide performance/security evidence.
Baseball section listing: representative section/index template.
Current high-school baseball story: representative article/detail and reading journey.
Search results for 大谷: representative query/form completion path.

findings.summary: The site remains light-only when the user requests dark mode.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually unchanged from the desktop capture; computed styles report color-scheme: normal and a transparent/light surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and retint surfaces, text, borders, and browser UI with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Canonical pages render a fixed desktop canvas scaled down on phones.
findings.evidence: At a 360x800 device viewport the layout primitive reports no viewport meta, a 980 CSS-pixel layout viewport, and scale 0.367; home, category, article, and search screenshots show tiny desktop text and controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and rebuild templates with fluid/intrinsic layout, responsive images, and component/container queries. Do not prevent zoom.

findings.summary: A sticky bottom advertising layer obscures article and listing content.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile captures show a dark fixed layer covering the bottom portion of the viewport, with only a small close affordance at the far edge.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the load-time obstruction or reserve non-overlapping space; if transient UI is essential, use a semantic, keyboard-operable, light-dismissible primitive.

findings.summary: Dense navigation, ads, rankings, job listings, and widgets compete with the news hierarchy.
findings.evidence: The first viewport has multiple navigation rows and a busy three-column composition; 394 requests include extensive advertising and recommendation infrastructure.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce secondary chrome, defer non-core modules, and establish a clear content hierarchy around headlines and article text.

findings.summary: Navigation and state changes use abrupt legacy swaps rather than view transitions.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found no view-transition CSS/API evidence, and routes are conventional MPA navigations with no cross-document transition declaration.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply progressive cross-document View Transitions to article/list navigation, with reduced-motion handling and a fallback.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-aware header or progress cue.
findings.evidence: The page exceeds 6,000 CSS pixels, while DOM/CSS inspection and screenshots show static chrome and no scroll progress or scroll-state treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: For long article pages, add a restrained scroll-state-aware header or reading-progress cue without increasing chrome.

findings.summary: Loading and interactivity are slow.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 4.2s, TBT 610ms, Speed Index 12.1s and time-to-interactive 32.7s; the CDP trace observed LCP 16.9s and 898ms total blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource, delay non-critical scripts and widgets, break long tasks, and remeasure on representative templates.

findings.summary: The page ships an excessive render and network dependency footprint.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 394 requests and 4.34MB transferred, including 110 scripts (2.44MB), parser-blocking legacy scripts, and missing cache headers on major resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or defer non-critical dependencies, load scripts with appropriate async/defer semantics, improve caching, and prioritise only the LCP image.

findings.summary: Large amounts of unused CSS and JavaScript are delivered.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 1,189KiB unused JavaScript and 176KiB unused CSS, while the HAR attributes 3.43MB to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit tag-manager and ad-tech payloads, conditionally load optional integrations, remove duplicate/legacy bundles, and split code by user-visible feature.

findings.summary: Important images and links lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed image-alt and link-name; the platform probe found unnamed logo/social links and images without alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Give linked images meaningful alt text or aria-labels, use empty alt only for decoration, and ensure every focusable control has an accessible name.

findings.summary: Text contrast and preference-adaptive contrast are insufficient.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found white #fff text on #9fb0bc at 2.23:1, below 4.5:1; no prefers-contrast/forced-colors adaptation was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise contrast to WCAG minimums and add forced-colors/prefers-contrast treatment that preserves controls and text.

findings.summary: Heading and landmark structure is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed heading-order; the DOM probe found no main landmark, an empty H1, a second H1, and skipped heading levels. Focus outlines were visible, but structure remains confusing.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one content H1, logical heading levels, and a main landmark while retaining the visible focus treatment.

findings.summary: Many controls are too small for reliable touch use.
findings.evidence: The platform probe counted 199 visible interactive elements below 24px in at least one dimension; scaling the desktop layout down makes targets still harder to acquire.
findings.suggestedFix: Use at least 24x24 CSS pixel targets (prefer 44x44 for primary touch controls), add spacing, and preserve non-hover and keyboard access.

findings.summary: Third-party integrations generate runtime and network errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse recorded CORS failures, failed resources, an OpenX JSON parse error, and an uncaught pa.sendEvents TypeError.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove failing integrations or isolate and guard them so optional ad/analytics failures do not produce uncaught exceptions.

findings.summary: Image and document asset hygiene is weak.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 18 images without dimensions, 14 oversized images, 59/59 in legacy formats, 31 below-fold images not natively lazy-loaded, and no responsive sources for 13 relevant images.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide dimensions/aspect-ratio, srcset/sizes and AVIF/WebP variants; use native lazy loading below the fold and correctly sized sources.

findings.summary: Canonical and sitemap indexing signals are incomplete.
findings.evidence: No canonical link was present on home, category, article, or search templates; /sitemap.xml returned 404. Raw HTML remained strong at 96% content coverage.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit self-referential canonical URLs for indexable templates and publish a sitemap index referenced from robots.txt.

findings.summary: Important browser security headers and cookie protections are absent.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are missing; 13 of 21 observed cookies lacked Secure and many used SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS and nosniff; add referrer/permissions policies and mark all HTTPS cookies Secure with the narrowest SameSite/HttpOnly settings.

findings.summary: The page has an unusually large tracking and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe found 78 third-party origins and 16 known tracker hosts; HAR recorded 314 third-party requests and 3.43MB transferred before user interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory every vendor, remove low-value trackers, obtain consent where required, batch analytics, shorten retention, and delay optional vendors until intent.

findings.summary: The visible account flow exposes no evidence of phishing-resistant authentication.
findings.evidence: Login/account surfaces and extensive Piano scripts are present, but DOM/source recon found no WebAuthn/passkey integration; no permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys/WebAuthn alongside account recovery and request any browser permission only after an explanatory user action.

findings.summary: The 404 state redirects users instead of offering durable recovery.
findings.evidence: /sitemap.xml returned a 404 document containing a timed AutoJump back to home, which can erase context before users inspect recovery options.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep error states stable, explain what failed, preserve the requested path, and offer explicit search, retry, back, and home actions.

findings.summary: Search input assistance is incomplete.
findings.evidence: The search form works, but its text input has no autocomplete token or explicit aria-label in recon; the UI relies on surrounding presentation.
findings.suggestedFix: Associate a visible label with the search field, provide a useful autocomplete/search token, and keep clear submit semantics.

findings.summary: Third-party code and oversized media dominate the page budget.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 314 requests and 3.43MB; three YouTube thumbnails alone exceed 500KB, while every inspected image uses a legacy format.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, defer recommendation/ad/media modules, serve appropriately sized modern image formats, and avoid loading below-fold thumbnails before need.

findings.summary: Content is server-rendered but intentionally unavailable to major AI agents and exposes no structured agent actions.
findings.evidence: robots.txt disallows GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, Google-Extended, anthropic-ai and Claude-Web; recon found no WebMCP/agentic tool registration. This is an emerging opportunity, not a conventional SEO failure.
findings.suggestedFix: If agent reach is a product goal, define an explicit crawler policy and expose safe structured actions or article affordances instead of requiring scraping.

findings.summary: Repeated scrolling is associated with substantial retained heap growth.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary reported 1,049,842 nodes and 52.9MB self size; after ten end-to-end scroll cycles the post summary reported 1,324,198 nodes and 65.4MB. Dynamic ad/feed caching may explain some growth, so leak attribution is medium confidence.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile repeated scrolling in one DevTools session, identify retained nodes/listeners/timers, cap caches, tear down observers, and retest after garbage collection.

taskList.title: Build genuinely responsive templates and restore readable mobile/zoom behavior
Cut the script, tracker, ad-tech, and third-party budget
Remove the content-obscuring sticky layer and simplify page chrome
Fix accessible names, heading structure, contrast, and search labelling
Profile retained heap growth during repeated scrolling
Add dark mode and preference-aware contrast
